# MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 Calibration checks - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Scope
This document describes calibration verification checks for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) following startup and after major maintenance. Checks focus on measurement systems and alarms that affect shot delivery, media recycling, and dust collection performance. Refer to SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-04, and SOP-P3-L1-05 for related operational and safety procedures.

Tools
- Handheld manometer compatible with target range for the dust collector pressure drop alarm
- Inspection mirror and flashlight
- Non-marring alignment probes and feeler gauge set
- Supply of lubricant: CFW-LUB-278
- Calibration tags and documentation forms

Procedure
- Visually inspect cabinet interior and media recycling components for wear or foreign material. Record observations on the calibration tag.
- Verify sensor mounts and wiring connections are secure and free of abrasion.
- Using the handheld manometer, measure across the dust collector differential element while the cabinet is at normal operating condition. Compare the measured value against the alarm setpoint for EQ-P3-L1-SB02.
- Confirm the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa. If measured value equals or exceeds the alarm point, follow escalation in SOP-P3-L1-04.
- Perform functional check of shot delivery sensors and media level indicators per the manufacturer's guidance and document results.
- Apply CFW-LUB-278 to specified mechanical bearings and linkage points where lubrication notes exist in the equipment history. Record lubricant serial or batch reference.

Acceptance criteria
- All instrument and alarm points return nominal readings and are mechanically secure.
- The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is set to and verified as 2025 Pa.
- Any deviation from expected readings triggers corrective actions per SOP-P3-L1-05 and is documented before returning the equipment to service.
